title: Batchwise Weight Streaming and KV Priming Orchestrator for Tenant-Scoped Warm Windows
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Motivation:
Large tenants and bursty workloads observe cold-start spikes when a model weight or KV context is not resident on a dedicated node. Existing warm-pool implementations pre-allocate nodes but do not coordinate fine-grained weight streaming or KV cache priming per-tenant priority windows. This ticket implements an orchestrator that performs batchwise weight streaming (chunked load with backpressure), prioritized KV prefetching (tenant scoring + bloom pre-seed), and a graceful admission controller that holds low-priority requests until their KV/weights reach an operational readiness threshold.

Scope:
- New controller that runs in the Dedicated control plane and issues per-fleet prewarm plans.
- Weight streaming agent: stream model shard chunks with RSVP-style pacing and early-decode health checks.
- KV priming stage: selective prime of prefixes and critical KV entries using scoring from historical prefix distribution.
- Admission controller hook for routing layer that returns 202 + warm-up hint or routes to compatible fallback model variant.
- Telemetry and guardrails for cost (tokens & GPU bandwidth) and latency SLOs.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of autoscaler policies (we add hooks and signals but do not replace autoscaler).
- Model format conversion or new quantization pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule a per-fleet prewarm job with tenant-priority weight
Weighted streaming reduces 95th->50th percentile weight-load time by >= 35% in lab tests
KV priming reduces first-request P99 latency for warmed prefixes vs cold baseline by >= 25%
Admission controller returns clear warm-up hints and routes to fallback when readiness < threshold
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating no more than 1.5x token-cost increase during a 5-minute prewarm window and SLOs met for P95 latency

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive priming reduces cold latency but increases token/GPU bandwidth and cost; we add per-tenant budget and time-boxing.
Fallback strategy: route to smaller compatible model variant with graceful degradation if readiness not met after configured timeout.
Observability: instrument chunk-level progress, estimated remaining bytes, and per-tenant priming score to support debugging and invoicing
